properties.title: Toward mechanistic medical digital twins: some use cases in immunology

membership.reason: Review and roadmap perspective summarizing forum discussions on mechanistic immune medical digital twins; does not implement or benchmark a new primary world model.
membership.counting_boundary: Excluded from primary implemented world models (not_world_model, BP_COMPONENT).

properties.backbone: Conceptual MDT roadmap (no single implemented primary model)

properties.flow: Conceptual workflow: biological data -> generic mechanistic model -> validation -> patient personalization -> clinical application

properties.purpose: Review and research roadmap for mechanistic immune medical digital twins.

assertions.rationale: Conceptual roadmap for personalized mechanistic medical digital twins in immunology.

evidence_fragments.content: It emerged from a two-day forum on problems related to medical digital twins, particularly those involving an immune system component.

[paraphrase (visual p.2)] Figure 1 shows the workflow for development of medical digital twins: disease-relevant human biological data -> generic computational model -> model validation -> model personalization -> model application, incorporating patient-specific data and patient population data.

locator.section_or_table: Examples of ongoing MDT projects (visual inspection)

evidence_fragments.content: We present a selection of ongoing projects by some of the Forum participants. The selection illustrates several disparate types of applications, methodologies, and uses. They are at different stages of development and collectively illustrate the issues we have raised in this meeting report/perspective. A summary of the projects presented at the Forum can be seen in Table 1.

capability_assessments.rationale: Review/perspective paper surveying mechanistic immune medical digital twin use cases and roadmaps without implementing a new primary world model (not_world_model).

limitations: Survey/perspective article only; no primary model implementation, dataset, or benchmark evaluation.
notes: All 9 physical PDF pages extracted/read; pages 2 (Figure 1), 4, and 5 (Table 1) visually inspected via rendered PNGs.
